default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-808.title: Lunch-range breakout
E-808.hypothesis: The thin midday hour builds a range of resting orders; a close beyond it after lunch shows the afternoon participants choosing a side, and stops beyond the range add fuel.

E-809.title: Alternating-colour chop break
E-809.hypothesis: A string of alternating bar colours is two-sided balance; the first close beyond the whole chop range ends the balance and follows through.

E-810.title: Keltner-envelope snapback
E-810.hypothesis: A close far outside an EMA envelope scaled by the average bar range is an overextension; the first bar back inside the envelope shows buyers/sellers of the extreme giving up.

E-811.title: Chandelier-level recovery follow
E-811.hypothesis: After a pullback deeper than k average ranges from the window extreme, a close back above that trailing level means trend holders have defended it; follow the recovery.

E-812.title: Persistent-body trend onset
E-812.hypothesis: When most of each bar's range is body over a window, moves are one-sided with little two-way trade; the onset of that state in the net direction continues.

E-813.title: Previous-close reclaim
E-813.hypothesis: The previous settlement-like close is a reference for overnight positions; after a spell on one side, a close back across it shifts the day's bias.

E-814.title: Close-line-break flip
E-814.hypothesis: A close beyond the extreme close of the last n bars flips a line-break trend state; the first flip shows the other side taking control.

E-815.title: Volatility-onset direction follow
E-815.hypothesis: When recent average bar movement jumps above the hour's norm, new information is being priced; the direction of the burst keeps going while liquidity is being consumed.

E-816.title: Thin volume-node crossing
E-816.hypothesis: Price entering a price bin where little volume traded today has few resting counterparties, so it tends to slide through to the next accepted area; follow the entry direction.

E-817.title: Range-multiple thrust bar
E-817.hypothesis: A close that moves more than the previous bar's whole range beyond its close is a thrust that overwhelms the prior bar's liquidity; follow.
